summary: 802.1X authentication failures and rate-limited RADIUS responses after radius config change
description:
Issue summary: After a scheduled RADIUS server configuration change deployed 2026-03-10 08:33 UTC, several employees reported failures authenticating to the corporate SSID (corp-wireless) and some VPN connections that rely on 802.1X machine auth. The failure mode appears as repeated EAP authentication timeouts and clients receiving Access-Reject after multiple retries.

Impact: Intermittent to sustained inability for affected users to join corporate Wi‑Fi (corp-wireless) and establish VPN tunnels using machine-based 802.1X. Impact started at ~08:40 UTC and affected approximately 12% of active Wi‑Fi authentication attempts in us-west region during the first hour. No billing/customer-facing impact.

Environment: Production (us-west) RADIUS cluster behind auth-lb-usw. Affected client OSes observed: macOS 13.6+, Windows 11. Network gear: Aruba APs running 8.10. RADIUS stack: FreeRADIUS derivative with custom rate-limiting module.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Attempt to join corp-wireless using machine 802.1X credentials (machine cert or machine AD credential) from an affected client.
2) Observe EAP timeout or Access-Reject in radiologs after 2-3 retries.
3) Attempt using personal device on corp-wireless (PSK) — usually succeeds.

Recent changes: On 2026-03-10 08:33 UTC, SRE deployed radius config changes to add stricter anti-replay and a global per-source rate-limit to mitigate a suspected brute-force vector. Change was rolled out via feature-flag to auth-lb-usw pool.

Hypothesis: The new global per-source rate-limit is too aggressive for bursts of legitimate machine authentication traffic (e.g., rekeys/roaming/AP re-associations), causing the RADIUS cluster to emit temporary Access-Reject or drop auth attempts and trigger client-side timeouts. This appears exacerbated by AP roaming flaps which create short bursty auth patterns.

Logs / Observations:
- auth-lb-usw/radius01 logs show lines: "RATE_LIMIT_DROP src=10.11.12.13 key=machine-identity count=23/20" around 08:39-08:42 UTC.
- Aruba AP debug shows repeated EAPOL-Start/EAPOL-Response exchanges during roaming windows.
- MacOS logs: "802.1X: Authentication timed out after 3 attempts".
- No increases in CPU or memory on radius instances; network telemetry does show spikes in auth packet rate from AP-controller cluster during the incident window.

Workaround: Temporarily rollback per-source rate-limit config on auth-lb-usw (done at 2026-03-10 09:05 UTC) which restored normal auth rates for affected clients. Temporary mitigation also included increasing window for RADIUS retry backoff on APs to reduce immediate re-auth bursts.

Resolution notes (so far): Rollback restored connectivity for most users. We need a safer rate-limit profile that distinguishes attacker-like patterns from normal roaming/rekey bursts.

Next steps / Action items:
- [P0] Create a controlled A/B rollout plan for revised rate-limit (SRE) — owner: Amina Patel — due 2026-03-13.
- Update runbook to include test harness for simulated roaming auth bursts (Network Eng) — due 2026-03-15.
- Add Prometheus alert for sustained RATE_LIMIT_DROP > 1% of auth requests over 5m (Observability) — owner: Samir Gupta.
- Postmortem draft and quad chart for Exec (Ops) — owner: Jordan Reyes — due 2026-03-17.

Linked references: Confluence runbook and change request, Slack thread #infra-wifi, PR that introduced rate-limiter.
